segments.text: In an autonomous first-order equation, the current state determines the direction of motion.
An equilibrium is a state where the derivative is zero. Nearby arrows describe local stability.
On the real line, a smooth autonomous flow cannot form a nonconstant periodic orbit.
At each state the vector field specifies one direction; a trajectory cannot return by reversing through the same states.
A harmonic oscillator needs position and velocity to specify its state.
Its phase space therefore has two dimensions even when its physical position lies on a line.
The real line and a circle have different topology. A direction field on a circle can support periodic motion.
Check the state variables, the equation assumptions, and the domain before using a result about one-dimensional flows.

requirements.title: Start with the state
requirements.objective: Identify the state variables and autonomous equation.
requirements.explanation: A state must contain enough information to determine the system's evolution. Establish that before counting dimensions.
requirements.practice: What information is needed to determine the next motion of an oscillator?

requirements.title: Reason about flows on a line
requirements.objective: Explain why a smooth autonomous flow on the real line has no nonconstant periodic orbit.
requirements.explanation: The vector field fixes the direction at each state. A returning orbit would require incompatible directions through the same states.
requirements.practice: Why does knowing only the physical direction of motion not establish the dimension of phase space?

requirements.title: Resolve the oscillator example
requirements.objective: Distinguish physical position from phase-space dimension and analyze an oscillator's phase portrait.
requirements.explanation: Position and velocity are separate state variables, so an oscillator's phase space is two-dimensional. The lesson explains this distinction but does not teach a complete phase-portrait construction.
requirements.gap: A worked phase-portrait construction is still needed.
requirements.practice: Name both state variables and explain why neither can be omitted.

requirements.title: Recognize a bifurcation
requirements.objective: Identify how equilibria change as a parameter varies.
requirements.explanation: This requirement needs a separate explanation and worked example. The inspected lesson does not establish it.
requirements.gap: No inspected clip covers parameter-dependent changes in equilibria.

video_summaries.summary: This authored example connects state variables, equilibria, nonperiodic flows on a line, and the oscillator's two-dimensional phase space. It also explains why the domain matters.
key_points: State dimension depends on the information needed to evolve the system.
Results about the real line do not automatically apply to a circle.
The oscillator is not a counterexample to the one-dimensional flow result.
